issue_title: [feaLib] possibly suboptimal compilation of inline multiple substitution rules
hints_text:
> Does my reasoning make sense? can we be more aggressive in reusing lookups in this case?

I think so. @simoncozens 
In theory this can be done with one lookup, yes. (Or fewer! It's possible to combine all non-overlapping "auxiliary" lookups which share the same lookup flags into a single lookup across multiple chaining rules.)

And yes, it makes sense that, because multiple `Rule` tables get generated, the impact of deduplication is limited to "leaf nodes".
> Or fewer! It's possible to combine all non-overlapping "auxiliary" lookups which share the same lookup flags into a single lookup across multiple chaining rules

I believe AFDKO does that? I thought feaLib does as well.
looks like feaLib builder always creates a new anonymous lookup for inline chained substitution rules, this method `get_chained_lookup_` always make a new one (unlike `get_lookup_` which attempts to reuse the current one where possible):

https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/blob/308b449edc940b9e9bb2368ac5c4afcf92e911e8/Lib/fontTools/feaLib/builder.py#L246-L251

https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/blob/308b449edc940b9e9bb2368ac5c4afcf92e911e8/Lib/fontTools/feaLib/builder.py#L1285-L1293

fea-rs has a `find_or_create_anon_lookup` method that takes two closures, one to check if a given existing lookup can be reused, another in case no suitable lookup is found to make a new one

https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc/blob/7511532553457fba90c4555ae111f5235446f399/fea-rs/src/compile/lookups/contextual.rs#L129

maybe we could take inspiration from that
